reverse_dcf_check: The engine says the 7.0x NTM EV/sales leg ($140.15) equals my DCF cash flows only at a ~5.1% WACC, against the 14.7% CAPM rate. At 14.7%, matching it needs a FY2030 exit of ~19.4x GAAP EBITDA instead of 14x (tested: 18x gives $131, 20x $144). That is ~7x FY2030 sales for a business then growing ~12% with ~22% GAAP EBIT and ~36% EBITDA margins, held through the OpenAI renewal around 2030-31: in effect growth above 15-20% well past 2030 or EBIT margins near 30%. That fits the bull case (OpenAI renews or expands, wafer-scale keeps a speed edge), not my base, given the renewal and competition risks in long_dated_risks. Why keep the leg at all: the peers it is drawn from also trade at multiples that imply discount rates far below their own CAPM rates (NVDA at ~27x EV/EBITDA on a 1.86 beta), so a CAPM-2.29-beta DCF sits systematically below where this cohort clears. Why cut it to 50% (from 60%, per the supervisor's challenge): the multiple leg is the optimistic one and I should not let it dominate. The 50/50 blend $122.77 embeds probability-weighted long-dated risk effects of about -$19/share (sum of long_dated_risks).

I removed the unconfirmed $273.6M RSU catch-up and rebuilt SBC from verified Q2 figures (RSU $332.9M, PRSU $34.2M), and added ~$265M of interest income the engine's bridge omits. Valuation: DCF $105.4 (14.7%, 14x FY2030 EBITDA) and 7.0x NTM EV/sales $140.15 (9-peer CY2027 median 10.0x after dropping ARM and ORCL), blended 50/50 (from 60/40, because the reverse DCF shows the multiple leg implies a 5.1% WACC) = $122.77, the engine base. Scenarios: bear $60.82 (25%: OpenAI shifts work, ramp slips, raise risk, neocloud multiple), base $122.77 (50%), bull $202.44 (25%: OpenAI expansion option, AWS/AMD channels, ~11x). Distribution: a mix of lognormals, sigma ~0.30-0.35 within each scenario, with slightly fatter tails than the engine for IPO-period volatility (115% realized, inflated). The ladder centres on ~$121 with P(>=149) = 0.35. It sits below spot because on my cash flows the price already discounts multi-year execution; the $292 average target from mostly underwriting banks is weak evidence. Thesis break $88 (~4.1x horizon NTM sales, neocloud level). Defense: not disclosed, at most 14% of FY2025 revenue, likely under 2%. The material weaknesses are confirmed in the 424B4 summary but kept out of the numbers.
